1 DEFINITIONS (fixed now)
1.1 Start, Birth, guard, lock, cut rule: as XS froze them (its 1.1-1.2), in my own code. Diamond torus n = 8 (1024 sites, 2048 links), A(x)-B(x-e_m). Birth: owner g, neighbours o_1..o_4,
    cut = (g,o_j) + (x_i,o_i) for i != j, x_i a neighbour of o_i other than g, {g,x_i} distinct; heir h joins g and the x_i; twin t joins o_1..o_4; child links copy the cut link's bit.
    GUARD exactly two of four cut links ON. LOCK: a cut containing a link with both ends LASTING is never offered. CUT RULE: admissible cuts, highest tight3 first, then the READING, ties uniform.
    The on-file second criterion (fewest uncovered loops) is not applied (as XS D1). No flips, no undo, no un-writing (modelling steps, as every growth protocol on file except TU's).
1.2 THE CANDIDATE DEFINITION UNDER TEST (PD-40; not adopted): every site carries a label; BOTH newborns of a Birth copy the label of the owner g. Labels never change otherwise (except scheme GPN).
    MIXED link = a link whose two ends carry different labels (label 0, 'unlabelled start material', counts as a label; the both-nonzero count is reported beside).
1.3 START LABELLINGS (all are INPUTS, counted; none chosen):
    EACH   every start site its own label (BFIN: every start site holds the right, so this is 'lineages from growth points' to the letter).
    HALF   label 1 if (i+j) mod 8 < 4 else 2 (two slabs, two flat walls; a supplied seam).      CUBE8  the eight octants of the torus (supplied seams).
    GP     (CP, FX) the 8 start growth points carry labels 1..8, every other start site label 0; a new growth point keeps the label it has.
    GPN    (CP) as GP, but a NEW growth point founds a new lineage: when it forms its site takes a fresh label (a modelling step; 'lineages from growth points' to the letter).
    VOR8   (CP, FX) every start site takes the label of the nearest start growth point (multi-source BFS, first reached; supplied seams).
    Under X0 the labels are passive, so one run carries all its body's schemes at once.
1.4 BODIES (start = XS's scrambled two-ON pattern: S order, then 20 x N alternating-loop flips; my own generator, so 'same seeds' means the same seed numbers, not the same streams):
    BFIN  XS's B-FIN: any-site supply with the sleep device, write rate w = 1, lasting chance p = 0.6 decided at the first write, lock, start sites never written or lasting. Seeds 18101, 18102.
    CP    XS's C': PD-17 books reading (PD-25 two carriers per new growth point, PD-30 any unfired site), k0 = 8, hop r = 10 along ON links, exclusion, release R1, GATE-A, park at 500 blocks,
          PD-18 heirs fire unwritten, w = 1, start written not lasting, lock with p = 0.25. Seeds 18311, 18312.
    FX    control, Part A only: 8 fixed growth points with heirs (PD-06/07A), no carriers, no writes, no lock: pure lines of descent. Seeds 25001, 25002. To 16x.
    XS's wall body A is NOT run (its growth-point rule is a rule change and XS found 99.9% of its Births on newborn material; budget) - a labelled omission.
    PIECES (for Part B) = connected clusters of lasting sites through locked links (TF D3, as XS). SOFT links = links that are not locked; soft sites = sites with at least one soft link.
1.5 READINGS (second criterion after tightness; none chosen)
    X0 none.  XSTALE (time mark, XS's): minimise max_i lastchange(x_i).  XFRESH (time mark, opposite): maximise it.
    HM1  eight-site handed-down read, XS's X1 form: maximise the number of mixed-label links among the four cut links (all their ends are among the Birth's own eight sites).
    HMK  eight-site read, seam-keeping: minimise Delta (1.6).   HMX  seam-thickening control: maximise Delta.
    HMK5 root + four neighbours only, unseen x_i assumed on its neighbour's side (SG checker's assumption): minimise 2 x #{i != j : label(o_i) != label(g)}.
1.6 HAND LEMMA (PROPOSED here; to be checked by recount at every Birth of every run): with both newborns copying the owner's label L,
    Delta(mixed links) = sum over i != j of T_i, T_i = [x_i != L] + [o_i != L] - [x_i != o_i] in {0,1,2}. So Delta >= 0 always, <= 6; Delta > 0 iff the Birth cuts a link foreign at both ends;
    Delta is fixed by the labels on the Birth's own eight sites. The mixed-link count M never falls; a seam is only diluted (+4 links per Birth).
1.7 MEASURES at every doubling k (N = 1024 x 2^k), per labelling scheme:
    M_k mixed links; m_k = M_k / all links; ms_k = soft mixed / soft links; mu_k = ms_k / (1 - sum of squared label shares) (1 = fully shuffled);
    gamma_k = log2(M_k / M_(k-1)) (seam exponent: 1 smear, 2/3 area law, 0 necks never grow); SEAM sites = sites with a mixed link; INT2_k = share of soft sites that are not seam sites and have
    no seam-site neighbour; COH = share of sites in the largest same-label connected cluster of their label; mean Delta per Birth and share of Births with Delta = 0 in the doubling;
    share of locked links that are mixed; share of pieces that are label-pure.
    VERDICT WORDS: SMEAR(k) iff INT2_k <= 0.10 and mu_k >= 0.5.  THIN(k) iff M_k <= M_0 x 2^(5k/6) (mean gamma <= 5/6, i.e. the mixed share falls at least half as fast, in logs, as an ideal
    3D seam) and INT2_k >= INT2_0.  Otherwise BROAD(k). (EACH/GP/GPN start with no seam; for them THIN needs gamma_k <= 5/6 over the last doubling and INT2_k >= 0.5.)
    COMMON MEASURES (guards): both rulers at the final size (label: rho and ball ratios on 16 seeded centres, as on file; walk: exact evolution from 8 late-born sources to t = 64, local slopes at
    4, 8, 16, 32, XS's plateau words; controls diamond n = 20, square sheet 128^2, random four-regular 16,384); PD-20 slices at the final size, two readings with the newest half of sites:
    W1 links with both ends newest-half, W2 links with at least one end newest-half (the two-layer window) - walk slopes, ball slope from the same centres, largest connected share;
    M3 old-pair stretch (24 start marks, mean form and median per pair, 4x-16x and 16x-64x); M4 the common still-interior measure: share of links present at the start of a doubling that are cut
    during it, by depth 0/1/2/3+ from the nearest growth point at its start (BFIN: every awake site is a growth point), also for start-start links, and the share of sites whose four slots never
    changed; fallback share; growth points k and beta.
    PART B MEASURES (XS's): D5 between-piece stretch = median per-pair exponent ln(D_64x/D_16x)/ln 4 over pairs of G4 (24 lasting sites drawn at 4x) lying in different pieces at both ends, plus
    the mean form and pair count; D4 = largest piece / lasting sites at 16x, 32x, 64x, FINITE iff it falls at both doublings (XS's letter; the shares reported beside); locked share.
    Added (mine): DL lineage stretch = the same exponent for 24 sites drawn at 4x, pairs with different labels at 4x, and same-label pairs separately.

2 STAGES AND GATES
 Stage 1, PART A to the spec's letter (passive labels, X0): BFIN and CP to 64x (they double as Part B's control), FX to 16x; two seeds each. Verdict words at two and at four doublings.
 Stage 2, PART A-ACTIVE (my registered extension): the seam with the preference ON, to 16x, two seeds: BFIN x {HM1, HMK, HMX} x {EACH, CUBE8} and HMK5 x CUBE8; CP x {HM1, HMK, HMX} x {GPN, VOR8}.
 GATE: Part B runs for a body iff THIN(4) holds in both seeds for some seam labelling of that body, either passively (the spec's letter) or with the handed-down reading on (my extension, labelled).
 Stage 3, PART B (gated): on each gated body, to 64x, two seeds: X0 (from stage 1), XSTALE, XFRESH, and every HM reading x scheme of stage 2 that is THIN(4) plus HM1 on the same scheme.
   Eight seeds (18103-18108 / 18313-18318) for a reading and its control when |raise - 0.05| < 2 SE (two seeds: SE = half-range), budget allowing; if not run, said so.
 If no gate opens, Part B is NOT run; if >= 300 CPU-s remain I may run ONE labelled ungated side-check (BFIN, HMK and HM1 on CUBE8, two seeds, to 64x); it cannot rescue the route.
 BUDGET: <= 1800 CPU-s in all (process time summed over processes); no new run launched after 1650. python3 -I, standard library only, own code, every version kept with sha256.
   Run lengths and the number of heavy-ruler runs are decided from smoke timings only (seed 7, unregistered, read for CPU time and validator flags only).

3 KILL CONDITION
 Spec, verbatim: "Mixed-label links spread through the whole soft space within two doublings, or the handed-down reading adds less than 0.05 to the between-piece stretch with the pieces finite."
 Operational (fixed now). CLAUSE 1 is judged on the supplied-seam labellings of XS's bodies under X0 (BFIN: HALF, CUBE8; CP: VOR8): MET iff SMEAR(2) in both seeds for every one of them;
 NOT MET iff THIN(4) in both seeds for at least one; otherwise BROAD - reported as 'partly', and then clause 2 or the gate decides. The to-the-letter lineage labellings (EACH, GP, GPN) are
 reported beside (they start fully mixed or seamless, so they cannot show a seam staying a seam).
 CLAUSE 2 (only if Part B runs): MET iff no HM reading raises D5 over X0 (seed means) by >= 0.05 with D4 FINITE in every seed and >= 20 pairs per seed and no stall. The time-mark readings
 are run beside as the comparison the spec names. A difference within two standard errors of zero is reported as no difference.
 THE ROUTE IS KILLED iff clause 1 is MET, or no gate opens (no thin seam, so Part B is not run), or clause 2 is MET. THE ROUTE SURVIVES only on a D5 raise >= 0.05 as above.
 Registered separately (not the spec's kill): 'pieces by lineage exist' iff some scheme is THIN(4) with COH >= 0.9 in both seeds, passively or actively.

method.summary: Own code (python3 -I, standard library). Growth by Births on a four-slot two-kind network with link bits, the two-ON guard, the lock on lasting sites and the tightest-first cut rule, in three supplies: BFIN (XS B-FIN: any site, lock, w = 1, p = 0.6), CP (XS C-prime: the principal's supply PD-17/25/30/18 with lock p = 0.25) and FX (eight fixed lines of descent, control). Every site carries labels in several start labellings at once; both newborns copy the owner's label. Part A follows mixed-label links (count, share, interior share, coherence) per doubling with no preference (the spec's letter) and with the handed-down preference on (registered extension). Part B (gated) compares the eight-site handed-down readings HM1/HMK(/HMK5, HMX control) with the time-mark readings XSTALE/XFRESH and the no-preference control on XS's between-piece stretch D5, same bodies and seed numbers.

results.headline: A seam stays a seam, and it buys nothing. (1) EXACT: with both newborns copying the owner's label, no Birth lowers the number of mixed-label links; the change is fixed by the Birth's own eight sites. (2) MEASURED, no preference: the seam does not smear - on every supplied-seam labelling the mixed share FALLS and the interior GROWS (two slabs, any-site body: mixed share 0.125 -> 0.063 at 64x -> 0.044 at 256x; sites more than one step from a seam site 0.50 -> 0.76 -> 0.84). Mixed links grow as N^0.75-0.80, a counting law (three of every four net links a Birth adds are mixed at the going rate), not an area law. (3) TO THE LETTER it fails under the principal's supply: if every new growth point founds a lineage, the label is fully mixed (share 0.78, interior 0.002). (4) The preference is a weak dial on the seam exponent (0.47-0.60 keeping, 0.84-0.87 thickening, against 0.70-0.77 with no preference, all over 16x-64x) and adds +0.012 +- 0.005 and +0.013 +- 0.010 to the between-piece stretch (0.05 needed), no better than time marks. Both rulers unchanged: walk 1.5-2.6 with no plateau near 3; label lost on the dense side in 30 of 30 runs.

R1_exact_seam_ledger.statement: Owner g with label L, neighbours o_1..o_4, own cut link (g,o_j), other cut links (x_i,o_i). Both newborns carry L. Then Delta(mixed links) = sum over i != j of T_i with T_i = [x_i != L] + [o_i != L] - [x_i != o_i], each 0, 1 or 2. Delta >= 0; Delta > 0 iff the Birth cuts a link foreign at both ends; Delta is a function of the labels on the Birth's own eight sites only.
R1_exact_seam_ledger.proof_sketch: Cut links mixed before: [o_j != L] + sum [x_i != o_i]. New links: heir-owner (never mixed), heir-x_i (mixed iff x_i != L), twin-o_i for all four (mixed iff o_i != L). The owner-link terms cancel; each remaining T_i is non-negative by the triangle inequality of the equal/unequal relation.

R3_the_three_quarter_law.explanation_PROPOSED: Per Birth the ledger gives Delta = 3 (a + b - c) where a, b, c are the chances that the far placed site differs from the owner, that a neighbour differs from the owner, and that a non-owner cut link is mixed. If each equals the going mixed share m, a Birth adds 3m mixed links per 4 net links, i.e. gamma = 3/4: one net link in four is the heir-owner link, pure by inheritance. Exact at the start of EACH (eight distinct labels give Delta = 3).

The far placed site (two steps away) is no more likely to be foreign than a neighbour: at the scale of one Birth the seam band is fully ragged. Where growth stays away from the seams the terms are below the going share (CP VOR8 seed 18311 early: 0.25-0.6, exponent 0.2-0.5; FX: 0).

plain_summary: Does a label that every newborn copies from the site that gave birth keep regions apart? We grew networks 64 times over and followed the links joining different labels. Exact: no Birth ever removes such a link; a boundary is only diluted. Measured: the boundary does not smear. Its share of links falls by about a sixth per doubling, and about four in five sites end up well inside one region. But if every new growth point starts its own label, everything mixes. A Birth can read the boundary exactly from its own eight sites, and preferring boundary-keeping cuts slows the boundary's growth. Yet this pushes still pieces apart by only 0.01, against the 0.05 needed, no better than time marks. The kill condition is met. Both rulers are unchanged: walk about 2, label lost on the dense side. One model family, unchecked, no card moved.
